To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
nesfatin is modulated by carbohydrate and fat intake.
carbohydrate, fat, protein and ghrelin modulate the expression and secretion of nesfatin1.
nesfatin is modulated by carbohydrate, fat and amino acids in vitro in stomach ghrelin cells, and by carbohydrate, fat, protein and amino acids in vivo in the mouse.
In summary, our research is concerned with
identifying dietary components that regulate nesfatin- 1, and the mechanisms involved.
identifying the mechanisms that regulate NUCB2 and nesfatin in the gut and liver.
the identification and characterization of novel anorectic factors, which may be involved in the control of food intake.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
carbohydrate and fat, but not protein, differentially regulate NUCB2 expression in vitro in MGN3 cells and in vivo in mice.
carbohydrate and fat suppress NUCB2 expression in vivo, while carbohydrate and fat increase NUCB2 in vitro in MGN3 cells.

glucose and amino acids stimulate NUCB2 and nesfatin expression, while fat inhibits NUCB2 expression and stimulates ghrelin expression in vitro in MGN3 cells, but in vivo, high fat diet causes a suppression of NUC2B expression in the stomach and large intestine, and a suppression of nesfatin in serum at the commencement of dark phase, and a suppression at 1 p. m. in mice fed a high carbohydrate diet.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
carbohydrate and protein stimulate, while fat inhibits NUCB2 and nesfatin1.
carbohydrate, fat, protein and amino acid differentially regulate NUCB2 and nesfatin 1.
glucose stimulates NUCB2 and nesfatin expression, while fat and protein inhibit NUCB2 expression.
The main takeaway from our work is that
carbohydrate, fat, and protein have differential effects on NUCB2 and nesfatin in vitro in cultured stomach ghrelin cells and in vivo in mice.
nesfatin is a meal responsive peptide and that its expression and secretion is modulated by carbohydrate, protein and fat.
nesfatin is a nutrient responsive peptide that is regulated by carbohydrate, fat and amino acid intake.
